review: Independent source and adversarial fixture review of the next 25 browser utilities

scope.method: Read all utility implementations and shared CSV parser; assert manually determined outputs, invariants, invalid-input refusals, metadata, and executable-looking input handling. Production module fixes were made by the source author after findings were relayed through the parent reviewer.

integrationSourceReview.finding: No additional material data loss or input defect identified in source inspection. This is not a substitute for browser interaction testing.
checks: The shared CSV parseCsv and csvToJson functions exactly match the committed implementation after newline normalization; the independent CSV regression suite passes after extraction.

BROWSER_TOOLS now contains all seven original routes plus all 25 new routes exactly once. The independent baseline uses the explicit original seven slugs, so inclusion of the new tools cannot invalidate the distinctness comparison.
ToolsPage keys BrowserTool by slug, so selecting a different tool remounts the parent input state and specialized form state together.
Text comparison retains separate before/after strings through JSON.stringify, including pasted newlines and quotes.
CSV column selection preserves pasted CSV and exact requested header spelling; the form explicitly documents one header per line.

Query parameter fields split at the first equals sign, preserve later equals signs and repeated values, construct own object properties safely, and disclose one key=value entry per line. Literal newlines in a key or value are outside that line-based form format.

Reading form updates retain other item fields and pass blank word counts as null for validation; blank/invalid speeds do not yield a valid schedule. List removal and addition explicitly update the output.
UTM fields serialize supplied campaign names as data rather than building URL text directly. Optional fields remain optional.
Rendered results use a pre text child. Download names use static route slug and extension metadata, rather than user-supplied filenames. Copy and download are disabled when an input error is present.

conclusion.distinctness: All 25 routes are unique and differ from the seven prior browser utilities and the calculator registry. Manual review finds practical distinct transformations or inspections, including reverse CSV conversion, column selection/profile/transpose, URL inspection and composition, code point inspection, Markdown extraction, reading allocation, and evidence-only action/time registers. This is a qualitative review, not a claim that the broader catalogue has no conceptual overlap.
conclusion.privacyAndExecution: The inspected module treats inputs as local data and has no fetching, evaluation, filesystem, account, messaging, or scheduling operations. Fetch/eval traps also remain untouched for executable-looking HTML, JSON, local-network URLs, and file links. Pasted secrets remain in the input/output strings; the tools do not remove them automatically.
conclusion.pathAndFilenameScope: No utility reads a supplied file or resolves a filesystem path. Unknown/path-like utility slugs are rejected; published slugs and extension metadata are constrained to safe static forms. Browser download integration and rendered result escaping require separate UI validation.

findingsResolved.problem: The original comparator sorted UTF-16 code units while the help promised Unicode code point ordering.
findingsResolved.fixture: U+E000 followed by U+1F600 on separate lines
findingsResolved.originalResult: The astral emoji sorted before U+E000.
findingsResolved.verifiedResolution: The code point comparator now places U+E000 first and retains repeated lines.

findingsResolved.problem: The original Number.isSafeInteger guard checked already-rounded values, silently changing fractional literals and underflowed numbers.
findingsResolved.originalResult: Long decimals rounded, a fractional value rounded into a safe integer, and 1e-400 became zero.
findingsResolved.verifiedResolution: A decimal normalization check rejects numeric literals that cannot survive conversion exactly, with instructions to quote such values. Quoted large identifiers remain unchanged.

findingsResolved.problem: An extra imported id column overwrote the generated row identifiers, allowing duplicate IDs.
findingsResolved.fixture: Two valid actions with the same extra CSV id value
findingsResolved.verifiedResolution: Generated identifiers are applied after imported fields and are 1 and 2.

findingsResolved.problem: Finite positive speed, duration and capacity could still produce an infinite totalMinutes, serialized as null.
findingsResolved.verifiedResolution: Nonfinite derived duration is rejected clearly. The separate 0.1 words/minute, one-minute, 1,000-word boundary fixture conserves words within tolerance and stays within 10,000 sessions.

limits: This report validates the pinned module through source inspection and Node fixtures. It does not assert browser integration, accessibility, browser download behavior, catalogue registration, deployment or live-site status.
Markdown utilities deliberately handle the documented subsets rather than all CommonMark constructs. Link inventory does not validate link availability or destination safety.
CSV formula protection deliberately prefixes formula-looking output cells with an apostrophe. This changes exported cell text to favor spreadsheet-safe imports and is disclosed in utility help.

The reading scheduler can return fractional-word segments for fractional capacity. Tests validate accounting within floating-point tolerance rather than promising physically indivisible word boundaries.
No broad fuzzing, million-character performance benchmark, external spreadsheet-application execution or model-generated outcome evaluation was performed.
